Okay, I've just finished a series of edits to the playtest script. First, I inserted the multiplayer section, spawning a second browser page (pageB) and establishing a DM room, then added checks to verify that both clients see each other. I also wrapped that visibility check in a loop to give the network time to propagate, replacing the previous single‑sleep approach. Next, I added a new scenario where the player stands near a patrolling bot to test whether the bot AI spots and engages the player, replacing the earlier screenshot‑tour HP check. Finally, I tweaked some existing checks (e.g., the sky‑view diff check) and left the rest of the test suite untouched.

Now I need to see whether these new checks are actually passing. Running the whole `node playtest.mjs` will generate a massive amount of output—everything from texture validation, SFX checks, map loading, bot navigation, character rendering, multiplayer sync, and the final “zero JS errors” summary. Scrolling through all of that manually would be tedious and error‑prone, especially since the output includes many lines that aren’t directly relevant to the new functionality I just added.

What I really care about are:
- Any failures (lines starting with the ✘ marker) that might indicate a regression.
- The new checks I introduced: the bot AI spotting the player, the “both clients see each other” multiplayer sync, the map loading messages (to confirm the map is correctly loaded), any bot navigation checks, character‑related checks, client A/B specific logs, cross‑client interactions, kill/scoreboard updates, victim handling, the overall “zero JS errors” check, and the remote player HP handling.
- Also, the generic “checks passed” line that the test harness prints at the end, to confirm the suite completed successfully.

To isolate these, I can pipe the test output through `grep -E` with a regex that captures either any failure marker (✘) or any of the specific success markers that contain the key phrases above. This will give me a concise view of just the relevant parts without drowning in noise.

I’ll run the test from the `test` directory, redirect stderr to stdout (`2>&1`) to catch any errors, and then filter with the constructed regex. Since the test can take a while (especially with the new multiplayer and bot AI loops), I’ll set a generous timeout of 7 minutes (420,000 ms) to ensure it has enough time to finish.

Thus, the appropriate next step is to execute this Bash command:
`cd /home/lane/AIArchives/archives/neonstrike/test && node playtest.mjs 2>&1 | grep -E '✘|✔ (bot AI spots|both clients|maps |map \"|bots navigate|character|client [AB]|cross-client|kill:|scoreboard|victim|zero JS|remote player)|checks passed'`.

This will re‑run the upgraded playtest and surface exactly the lines I need to verify the new functionality.
